title: 10 Best Investments: Where to Invest in 2026
author: Sigma Capital
metaDescription: In 2026, consider high-yield savings accounts, bonds, and S&P 500 index funds for balanced returns. Mutual funds and REIT index funds also offer diversification
excerpt: In 2026, consider high-yield savings accounts, bonds, and S&P 500 index funds for balanced returns. Mutual funds and REIT index funds also offer diversification and growth potential. Bitcoin ETFs and small-cap funds carry higher risk but promise significant rewards.

content.introduction: In 2026, consider high-yield savings accounts, bonds, and S&P 500 index funds for balanced returns. Mutual funds and REIT index funds also offer diversification and growth potential. Bitcoin ETFs and small-cap funds carry higher risk but promise significant rewards.
body:
The list below, from Bankrate's guide to the best investments for 2026, spans the full spectrum from capital preservation to aggressive growth. It starts with the safest vehicles — accounts and instruments backed by federal insurance — and moves through bonds, dividend funds, index funds, and finally to the most volatile option on the menu. Each carries its own risk-reward profile, and none is universally right or wrong. [...] The Nasdaq$NDAQ-100 includes prominent companies such as Apple $AAPL, Alphabet $GOOGL, and Microsoft $MSFT, giving investors concentrated exposure to the technology sector's long-term growth potential. That concentration cuts both ways: valuations tend to be high, meaning these stocks can fall sharply in downturns but also recover quickly when sentiment improves.

## 10. Bitcoin ETFs

Cheng Xin / Getty Images [...] Small-cap funds invest in the stocks of relatively small companies, many of which are earlier in their growth trajectories than the market's established giants. Investors must be prepared to hold through significant volatility, but the best small-cap ETFs have delivered double-digit annual returns over extended periods, rewarding those with patience and a long time horizon.

## 7. REIT index funds

Thana Prasongsin / Getty Images

Wondering where to invest your money this year? High-yield savings accounts, CDs, bonds, funds and stocks are all considered among the best investments available. Learn more about the risks, potential returns and how to get started.

 and covered the stock market, investing strategies, investment accounts and cryptocurrency. His work has appeared in The Associated Press, The Washington Post, MSN, Yahoo Finance, MarketWatch, Newsday and TheStreet. [...] High-yield savings accounts: 3% to 4%+.
 CDs: 3% to 4%+, depending on term.
 Bond mutual or index funds: 3% to 4% for U.S. government bonds; more for riskier bonds.
 S&P 500 (an index of U.S. large-cap stocks): 10% long-term historical average annualized return.

How do I know which investment is best for me?How do I know which investment is best for me?

When choosing an investment type, you'll want to consider your risk tolerance and how soon you'll need the money. [...] ## 6. Mutual funds

A mutual fund pools cash from investors to buy stocks, bonds or other assets. Mutual funds offer investors an inexpensive way to diversify — spreading their money across multiple investments — to hedge against any single investment’s losses.
